transcript:
Header: Date: 2026-03-12 | Start: 14:00 UTC | Duration: ~45m | Recording: on
Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE), Ethan Liu (Redwood SE), Priya Kapoor (Orion, ML Eng), Liam O'Connell (Orion, Platform), Sara Mendel (Orion, Head of Data)
Shared: deck (drive link), benchmark spreadsheet (sheet link), security pack (link)

Summary: quick sync on model selection, pinning plan, rollback/fallback strategy after last week's throughput anomalies; confirm next steps for benchmarks and security review.

00:00 Speaker 1 - Ava: all right hey everyone thanks for joining, um we'll keep this to 45 minutes. Quick agenda? model selection follow-up, pinning/rollout, canary strategy, and outstanding security items. Priya you mentioned some new failure cases in the sheet?
00:18 Speaker 2 - Priya: yeah thanks Ava, um we've been running more of the transaction summarization tests and saw a spike in hallucinations with the smaller quantized models, like q4b and q8_0, at longer contexts. There's a set I uploaded this morning, names start with "txn-edge-".
00:37 Speaker 1 - Ava: got it. Ethan can you give us the runtime/latency picture after the infra tweak last week?
00:44 Speaker 3 - Ethan: sure — so we re-ran the 1k and 2k prompt batches on hostdedicated and, uh, on the dedicated pool. The dedicated pool is still giving us more consistent p99, about 220 to 250ms token p99 for the baseline unquantized model. For q4b pinned models we saw token p99 around 280 to 340ms depending on sequence length; throughput improved a bit but quality dipped in those edge cases. There's also some inference jitter when we hit 2k seq because of KV cache evictions.
01:19 Speaker 4 - Liam: when you say KV cache evictions, you mean the KV cache memory pressure on the instance? is that tuned automatically?
01:26 Speaker 3 - Ethan: yeah, exactly — at longer contexts the K V cache (sometimes shows up as "K V cash" in the telemetry) gets flushed more often. The runtime has policies but on smaller GPU types we hit memory thresholds. We can reserve more memory or change the kernel packing, but that increases cost or may require a different instance size.
01:45 Speaker 2 - Priya: is that something Redwood Optimize can suggest? cache/batching profiles?
01:51 Speaker 3 - Ethan: we can, Redwood Optimize does give batching and caching suggestions but for the POC we recommended pinning a slightly larger model variant that keeps contextual fidelity without full float32 cost. So far the catalog candidates are: rwd-large-v1 (baseline), rwd-medium-q4b (quantized), rwd-medium-q8_0, and rwd-small-fast. The team tested rwd-medium-q4b and rwd-large-v1.
02:18 Speaker 1 - Ava: quick clarify — when we say "pinning" we mean pin traffic to a specific model version in config so it doesn't float on auto-route, correct?
02:25 Speaker 3 - Ethan: yes, pin = model_version pin in route config. We also recommended a fallback policy: primary pinned = rwd-medium-q4b-2026-02-28, fallback = rwd-large-v1-2026-02-15. If p99 latency or quality delta exceed thresholds route switches to fallback.
02:46 Speaker 5 - Sara: can you remind us of the quality delta threshold you recommend? We need concrete numbers for our SLOs.
02:53 Speaker 3 - Ethan: recommended is <= 5% drop in ROUGE/mean-EM on our eval set; for hallucination rate increase no more than +2% absolute. Those are tunable but starting point.
03:05 Speaker 2 - Priya: the problem is some of our critical regulated workflows can't tolerate hallucinations at all — even +1% is bad for the compliance team. So we need strict fallback when any hallucination is detected on a sample set.
03:18 Speaker 1 - Ava: understood, for regulated pipelines we can do stricter canary sampling and immediate rollback if criteria met. We should plan a safety canary: 5% traffic, run for 24 hours with daily checks and abort if any of the sampled transactions show hallucination.
03:33 Speaker 4 - Liam: from infra side we also need to talk about VPC/private deployment — some of the data can't leave their subnet. Where are we on Private deployment timeline?
03:44 Speaker 1 - Ava: our Private offering requires a short enterprise onboarding; we can provide a VPC peering model and bring the control plane in your account. For the POC we agreed to run on Redwood Dedicated with encrypted at-rest and ingress E2E, but if you want full private we need security review and a slightly longer timeline.
04:03 Speaker 5 - Sara: the CISO will insist on KMS/HSM integration and full audit logs. Do you have those?
04:10 Speaker 1 - Ava: yes we integrate with customer KMS for key wrapping and have audit logs. I'll attach the SOC2 and HSM notes after the call.
04:20 Speaker 2 - Priya: one more on model comparisons — can you share the catalog comparison sheet with latencies and quality metrics? The sheet you sent had some missing columns.
04:29 Speaker 3 - Ethan: I'll update the benchmark sheet. Current table: model, quant, p50 token latency, p95, p99, tokens/sec, eval-rouge, hallucination-rate. I'll fill in the missing p95 for q4b and include sequence-length buckets (512/1024/2048).
04:46 Speaker 1 - Ava: perfect. On rollouts — what does rollback look like operationally? If we do a canary and see failures, can you walk through steps?
04:54 Speaker 3 - Ethan: operation is automated at the route layer — we have health checks and a scoring probe that runs a small eval set. If the scoring probe crosses thresholds a route rule flips to fallback model instantly, and alerts are pushed to PagerDuty/email. We can also schedule an automated rollback window if the canary fails more than X times. Manual rollback is one click in the console.
05:20 Speaker 5 - Sara: what about auditability? we need to trace which model version served which request for at least 90 days.
05:27 Speaker 3 - Ethan: we log model_version_id per request and keep request metadata; retention depends on plan but we can export logs to your S3 for retention beyond default retention. Also we can include token-level cost breakdown for replay.
05:44 Speaker 2 - Priya: are there privacy or PII masking features? some of these transactions include account numbers.
05:51 Speaker 1 - Ava: we have configurable pre-processing hooks and redaction in the pipeline; we can also do local pre-filtering in your VPC.
05:59 Speaker 4 - Liam: coming back to the performance anomalies last week — any hypothesis why q4b appeared stable on your side but we saw degradation? Could be GPU kernel selection mismatch?
06:09 Speaker 3 - Ethan: possible — kernel selection can vary by infra; also compiler heuristics for attention can change with sequence length. Another possibility: batching patterns in your traffic created hot tails and caused cache churn. We need to replicate your traffic mix in the benchmark.
06:28 Speaker 2 - Priya: I'll provide production traffic sample (anonymized) — about ~30k requests/day right now, typical seq length 700 median, tail at 2k.
06:36 Speaker 1 - Ava: that's helpful — we should prioritize 1) benchmarking q4b vs rwd-large-v1 on your traffic sample 2) run a canary with strict hallucination checks 3) adjust batching/caching profiles and re-run.
06:51 Speaker 5 - Sara: security-wise send the SOC2 and network diagrams and also confirm SSO/SAML support for our users.
06:59 Speaker 1 - Ava: yes SSO/SAML supported, RBAC roles available. I'll include that in the packet.
07:06 Speaker 4 - Liam: about cost — if we pin to rwd-large-v1 what's the delta vs q4b? We need estimates for committed capacity vs usage.
07:15 Speaker 3 - Ethan: rough rule: unquantized large model about ~2.8x token cost vs q4b medium. But because of better quality and fewer re-runs, end-to-end cost delta is often smaller. I'll add a cost-per-1M tokens table.
07:31 Speaker 2 - Priya: can we set up the canary so that failed samples are automatically routed to a human-in-the-loop queue for quick triage?
07:38 Speaker 3 - Ethan: yep that's supported — webhook to your triage system or send to a small review queue in the console. We'll add that to the canary config.
07:47 Speaker 1 - Ava: good. Any blockers from the Orion side for the next week?
07:51 Speaker 2 - Priya: just me uploading the failing prompts and the prod sample; I should have them by Monday.
07:56 Speaker 5 - Sara: final: we'll want the security review before committing to any reserved capacity.
08:01 Speaker 1 - Ava: understood — schedule that once Liam and I sync on available times.
08:05 Speaker 3 - Ethan: quick note — for rollback/fallback naming, we're recommending the canonical flow: route.primary = rwd-medium-q4b-2026-02-28 (pinned), route.fallbacks = [rwd-large-v1-2026-02-15], and a secondary fallback of rwd-small-fast for cost-critical low-quality paths. You can also configure multi-tier fallback (dedicated -> hosted -> small-fast).
08:35 Speaker 4 - Liam: about multi-tier — does the routing support regional fallbacks? if eu-east is saturated, can we failover to eu-west or to hosted?
08:43 Speaker 3 - Ethan: yes routing policies support region and capacity tier fallback with automatic capacity checks; you can set policy precedence. We'll include example configs.
08:55 Speaker 2 - Priya: testing plan — can we do a 10% canary for 48 hours with daily quality reports and immediate rollback on any hallucination in the regulated workflow?
09:04 Speaker 1 - Ava: yes 10% 48h with strict halt-on-hallucination for regulated flows, for non-regulated we can do 24h. We'll document both.
09:12 Speaker 5 - Sara: ok sounds good. Also request that we get a sample of raw logs for a failed run for our auditors.
09:19 Speaker 3 - Ethan: we can export redacted raw logs to your S3; I'll set a lifecycle and masking rules.
09:26 Speaker 1 - Ava: great, let's recap next steps — Ethan update benchmark sheet and run replication on provided traffic sample; Priya upload failing prompts and prod sample; Ava send quote and security pack; set security review meeting. We'll reconvene same time next week.
09:46 Speaker 2 - Priya: thanks all, appreciate it.
09:49 Speaker 1 - Ava: thanks everyone, closing now.

Action items (in transcript): Ethan to update benchmarks and run 2k-sample replication; Priya to upload failing prompts; Ava to send SOC2 + network diagrams + pricing; schedule security review.

Notes: transcription contains occasional mis-heard tokens (e.g., "K V cash" for K V cache, "hostdedicated" instead of "hosted/dedicated").

References: deck link: https://drive.example/rwd-orion-poc-deck, benchmarks: https://sheets.example/orion-benchmarks, security pack: https://files.example/redwood-security-pack
